subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements about magnetic field due to a bar magnet:

(a) The field lines inside a bar magnet are directed from its south pole to the north pole.

(b) The magnetic field lines exist only outside the bar magnet.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only (a)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Magnetic field lines** inside a bar magnet are directed from its **south pole to the north pole**.
 
• **Magnetic field lines** also exist **inside the bar magnet**, not just outside it.
 
• The correct statement here is **(a)**, indicating the direction of magnetic field lines inside the bar magnet.
 
• Statement **(b)** is incorrect as it falsely claims that magnetic field lines exist only outside the bar magnet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic field lines** are continuous and form closed loops.
 
• Outside the bar magnet, magnetic field lines travel from the **north pole to the south pole**.
 
• The concept of magnetic field lines helps in visualizing the strength and direction of the magnetic field.
 
• A bar magnet has a **dipole field**, meaning it has two poles: north and south.
 
• Magnetic fields are vector fields, which means they have both magnitude and direction.
